correctness.rationale: The Schur norm is exactly a maximum of weighted nuclear norms by duality. Joint concavity of matrix fidelity makes averaging over the defect stabilizer valid and permits \(p=q\) by symmetry. The reduced Gram spectrum consists of N with multiplicity \(N-2\) plus an explicitly computed \(2\times2\) block. Its trace norm has a unique analytic maximizing parameter and yields the stated closed form and asymptotic. A standalone standard-library checker passes 560 finite assertions, which are supplementary only.

evidence: Holbrook–Johnston–Schoch prove the general upper bound \(\sqrt N\) and equality iff Hadamard; this bounds but does not determine the strict defect loss.
Davidson–Donsig exact symmetry theorem assumes transitive group action, while defect-preserving action has two distinct orbits (zero and nonzero).

Christensen 2026 Theorem 2.2 characterizes all self-adjoint Schur norms as an implicit positive-matrix optimization; it contains no closed-form Walsh one-defect specialization or dimension asymptotic.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Hadamard upper bound has broader matrix scope but cannot imply the exact strict deficit and its optimizer. The transitive Schur norm formula does not subsume the two-orbit defect calculation without the new concavity reduction. A general abstract SDP representation does not give the closed form. Christensen's general self-adjoint semidefinite representation supplies a different implicit optimization but no exact evaluation for the specified matrix family.

originality.rationale: Full relevant text of the 2022 sharp real sign-matrix Schur norm paper and 2005 symmetry foundations, and the 2026 revision of a general self-adjoint variational representation, were compared by implication. The known order-four value and general \(\sqrt N\) Hadamard equality case are credited; none of the inspected theorems supplies the all-dyadic sharp one-defect formula, weight optimizer or \(N^{-3/2}\) stability law. Indexed mathematical-finding alias searches found no equivalent record; unindexed prior derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent one-sign-defect Walsh/Schur norm identity may appear in earlier nearly-Hadamard, factorization, matrix-balancing or operator-space literature not indexed by the available sources.
The uniqueness of the optimizer is established only inside the symmetry-reduced family; arbitrary non-symmetric optimizers are not classified.

value.rationale: The sharp Hadamard Schur norm is an extremal benchmark. One flipped sign is the simplest meaningful perturbation of this benchmark; the result measures its exact effect throughout an infinite family and shows a nontrivial \(N^{-3/2}\) deficit with explicitly optimized adversarial weight distributions. The result is not merely a numerical recomputation of a fixed small order.
